_why: 867-G3 measured that agents/top.md's heading -- 'Build-safe agents (MIT / Apache-2.0 /
BSD / ISC / 0BSD)' -- governs 303 of the 543 rows the count gate credits to that page.
The other 240 sit in tables under PASS headings, which name no grant, so the shelf's
licence promise was structurally UNREACHABLE for 44% of its own counted rows.
repos/foundations.md (390 rows) and verticals/solutions.md (229) state no predicate at
all and correctly abstained entirely.
867-G3 offered three repairs and required that the choice be STATED, not drifted into.
p868 chose (c) -- 'require every counted holdings table to sit under a predicate-bearing
heading' -- because it is the only one of the three that closes the CLASS rather than
the instance, and folded in (a) for the vocabulary.
HOW (c) IS IMPLEMENTED, and why not literally. Taken literally, (c) means editing 24+
historical PASS headings to append a parenthesised grant set. That rewrites the
published record of earlier passes to satisfy a gate -- the defect p718 named as
'keying a gate on prose', committed deliberately. So the predicate is declared HERE,
per shelf FILE, machine-readable and in one place. Every counted row is then gradeable
by construction, which is (c)'s guarantee; a table whose own heading states a
parenthesised grant set still overrides the file default, because that is strictly more
specific. No historical heading is touched.
(a) IS FOLDED IN AND SAID OUT LOUD. The build-safe vocabulary was five names and
867-G3 showed it under-inclusive: MulanPSL-2.0 (OSI-approved, permissive) and WTFPL
(public-domain-equivalent) are build-safe in substance and were scored VOCAB-MISS.
ECL-2.0 is added for the same reason and with a specific stake in this industry -- the
Educational Community License is an Apache-2.0 derivative written FOR this sector, and
this base already shelves sakaiproject/sakai and opencast/annotation-tool under it.

agents/top.md.note: The shelf's client-facing promise: a row here can be built on and shipped in a client deliverable without a copyleft obligation travelling with it.

repos/foundations.md.note: No licence predicate, and that is a POSITION rather than an omission: a foundational repo is cited for what it establishes in the industry, and Moodle's GPL-3.0 or Open edX's AGPL-3.0 does not stop it being foundational. A row's grant is still byte-read and published; it is just not a filter here.

verticals/solutions.md.note: Copyleft is admitted BY OBLIGATION, which is p866's finding: a Moodle plugin links against Moodle and is GPL-3.0 because the platform is, not because the author chose it. Filtering copyleft off this shelf would delete the Moodle and Open edX estates, which are most of the sector.

excluded_everywhere.note: `not_open_source` is the T250 class: a grant whose bytes sit near a permissive payload's size and whose GitHub FIELD often reads NOASSERTION. p868 byte-read Oriole-FDU/Wisepen at 4,539 B and found Business Source License 1.1 behind a NOASSERTION field; p867 found Elastic-2.0 behind one on canyongbs/advisingapp.
